translationRepairs: The Emperor Yuan's taboo name was Rui, his courtesy name Jingwen; he was a great-grandson of Emperor Xuan and the son of Prince Gong of Langye, Jin.
The Emperor Yuan's taboo name was Rui, his courtesy name Jingwen; he was a great-grandson of Emperor Xuan and the son of Jin, Prince Gong of Langye.
The final 覲 is the personal name Jin of Prince Gong of Langye, not the dynasty; trailing 'Jin' after the title misreads it as a polity.
Hua Yi, the Jiangxi governor, refused to fall in line, so he dispatched Zhou Guang of Yuzhang and the former governor Wei Zhan to bring him in by force.
Hua Yi, the Jiangzhou governor, refused to fall in line, so he dispatched Zhou Guang of Yuzhang and the former governor Wei Zhan to bring him in by force.
江州 is the Jin province Jiangzhou; Jiangxi is a later geographic name.

He sent his generals to secure the lower Yangzi region, executed the turncoat Sun Bi at Xuancheng, crushed Du Tao's rising in Hunan, and on delegated authority proclaimed an amnesty for Jingzhou and Yangzhou.

He sent his generals to secure the lower Yangzi region, executed the turncoat Sun Bi at Xuancheng, crushed Du Tao's rising in Xiangzhou, and on delegated authority proclaimed an amnesty for Jingzhou and Yangzhou.
湘州 is the province Xiangzhou; Hunan is an anachronistic substitution.

On the bingyin day in the sixth month, Liu Kun—minister of works, governor of Bingzhou, and marquis of Guangwu—joined Duan Pidi, governor of Youzhou and duke of Bohai; Liu Han, Wuhuan commandant and general who guards the north; the chanyu and duke of Guangning, Duan Chen; Duan Juan, duke of Liaoxi; Shao Xu, governor of Jizhou and lord of Zhu'a; Cao Yi, governor of Qingzhou and marquis of Guangrao; Liu Yan, governor of Yanzhou and marquis of Dingxiang; Cui Bi, colonel of the eastern Yi; Murong Hui, commander-in-chief of the Xianbei; and one hundred seventy-two other notables in a joint memorial pressing him to take the throne. They wrote:

On the bingyin day of the sixth month, Liu Kun—Minister of Works, governor of Bingzhou, and Marquis of Guangwu—together with Duan Pidi, governor of Youzhou, Worthy King of the Left, and Duke of Bohai; Liu Han, Commandant for Protecting the Wuhuan and General Who Guards the North; Duan Chen, Chanyu and Duke of Guangning; Duan Juan, Duke of Liaoxi; Shao Xu, governor of Jizhou and Viscount of Zhu'a; Cao Yi; Liu Yan; Cui Bi; Murong Hui; and the other signatories—one hundred eighty men in all—submitted a memorial urging him to take the throne:
等一百八十人 states a total of one hundred eighty, including the named men; subtracting them to invent 172 others is unsupported.

Since the Yuankang era troubles have multiplied; by Yongjia the air itself seemed poisoned with rebellion. The Son of Heaven lost his grip, barbarian pretenders seized the capital, and the dynasty hung by a thread like the king's tassels swaying over his brow.

Since the Yuankang era troubles have multiplied; by Yongjia the air itself seemed poisoned with rebellion. The polar throne lost control, the emperor died among barbarian peoples, and the state's peril was like dangling tassels.
宸極失御 is loss of control of the polar throne; 登遐醜裔 records the emperor's death among barbarian peoples, not pretenders seizing the capital.

From Yuankang onward, hardships repeatedly arose; at the Yongjia juncture, miasma and pestilence grew ever darker; the polar throne lost control; ascended distant ugly descendants; the state's danger was like dangling tassels.

From Yuankang onward, hardships repeatedly arose; at the Yongjia juncture, miasma and pestilence grew ever darker; the polar throne lost control; he passed away among the barbarian tribes; the state's danger was like dangling tassels.
登遐 is an imperial death formula and 醜裔 a pejorative for barbarian tribes, not a literal ascent of ugly descendants.

Since the heartland fell the nine provinces have shattered and the empire roams uprooted with nowhere to lay its loyalty. The barbarian Yi who seized Xia and the Quanrong who drove out the Zhou were trifles beside this.

Since the heartland fell the nine provinces have shattered and the empire roams uprooted with nowhere to lay its loyalty. Xia's suffering under the archer Yi and the Zhou house's expulsion by the Quanrong were trifles beside this.
夷羿 is the archer Yi who usurped Xia; 夷 is part of the epithet, not an ethnic label 'barbarian Yi'.

Your subject, presenting a memorial envoy returning, then received that the western court in last year's eleventh month was not guarded; the lord above was secluded and seized; again he sank in the barbarian court; the divine vessel drifted apart; twice humiliated by wild rebels.

Your subject, when the envoy sent with a memorial returned, then received that the western court in last year's eleventh month was not held; the lord above was secluded and seized; again he sank in the barbarian court; the divine vessel drifted apart; twice humiliated by wild rebels.
臣奉表使還 means the memorialist's envoy returned, not that the subject himself was the envoy.

Now the ancestral temple is cut off and ended; the hundred million lack attachment; the host of officials and multitude of directors all press him with the great government; how dare I decline; respectfully I follow what is held."

Now the ancestral temple is cut off and ended; the hundred million lack attachment; the host of officials and multitude of directors all press me with the great government; how dare I decline; respectfully I follow what is held."
The edict is first-person (孤/予); 咸勉之以大政 is pressed upon the speaker, so 'him' reverses the person.

So I ascended the southern altar, received the abdication as did the kings of old before the spirit of King Wen, burned the offering kindling, displayed the auspicious tokens, and reported to High Heaven according to the rite.
So I ascended the southern altar, received the succession before the Wen Ancestor, burned the offering kindling, displayed the auspicious tokens, and reported to High Heaven according to the rite.
受終文祖 is the classical accession formula at the Wen Ancestor, not abdication before King Wen.
On the jiashen day Diao Xie rose from left vice director to director of the secretariat, while Xun Song, the general who pacifies the south and marquis of Quling, was named left vice director.
On the jiashen day Diao Xie rose from left vice director to director of the secretariat, while Xun Song, the general who pacifies the south and duke of Quling, was named left vice director.
曲陵公 is a ducal title (公), not a marquisate (侯).

Two-thousand-bushel commanders and magistrates ought reverently to uphold old statutes, correct the body and clarify the law, suppress and equalize powerful magnates, preserve and pity orphans and solitaries, conceal and verify household registers, encourage and supervise farming and sericulture.

Two-thousand-bushel commanders and magistrates ought reverently to uphold old statutes, correct the body and clarify the law, suppress and equalize powerful magnates, preserve and pity orphans and solitaries, ascertain and verify household registers, encourage and supervise farming and sericulture.
隱實戶口 means to bring hidden households to light and verify the registers, not to conceal them.
Welcoming the catalpa palace at Pingyang, was not able and returned.
They went to welcome the catalpa coffin at Pingyang, were unable to succeed, and returned.
梓宮 is the late emperor's coffin; the original line also lacks a grammatical subject for 迎…不克而還.
Zhou Fu, interior governor of Pengcheng, killed Zhou Mo, interior governor of Peiguo, on a charge of rebellion.
Zhou Fu, interior governor of Pengcheng, killed Zhou Mo, interior governor of Peiguo, and rebelled.
殺…以反 means Zhou Fu killed Zhou Mo and rebelled, not that Zhou Mo was executed on a charge of rebellion.
On guichou in the fifth month the Taiyang mausoleum fell in; again the emperor donned mourning white and wept three days.
On guichou in the fifth month the Taiyang mausoleum fell in; the emperor donned mourning white and wept three days.
The Chinese has no 又 or other marker of repetition; 'again' is invented.
On the bingzi day in the sixth month Zhou Fang was additionally named general who guards the south.
On the bingzi day in the sixth month Zhou Fang was additionally named General Who Pacifies the South.
安南將軍 is General Who Pacifies the South; 安 is not the garrison verb 鎮.
In the sixth month on bingzi he added Zhou Fang as General Who Guards the South.
In the sixth month on bingzi he added Zhou Fang as General Who Pacifies the South.
The same office 安南將軍 should be Pacifies the South, not Guards the South.
On bingyin in the fifth month Sima Quan, the late Emperor Huai's crown prince, was murdered at Pingyang; the court kept three days of mourning.
On bingyin in the fifth month Sima Quan, the late Emperor Huai's crown prince, was murdered at Pingyang; the emperor wept three days.
帝三日哭 makes the emperor the mourner; 'the court' changes the subject.
Zhou Fang, governor of Liangzhou and general who guards the south, died on the xinwei day.
Zhou Fang, governor of Liangzhou and General Who Pacifies the South, died on the xinwei day.
The office held at death is 安南將軍, not a 'guard the south' title.
On xinwei, Inspector of Liangzhou, General Who Guards the South Zhou Fang died.
On xinwei, Inspector of Liangzhou, General Who Pacifies the South Zhou Fang died.
Literal English must match 安南將軍 as Pacifies the South.
The crown prince performed the capping rite at the imperial university.
The crown prince performed the libation offering at the imperial university.
釋尊 at the 太學 is the school libation (釋奠), not the capping rite.
The imperial heir apparent released the cap at the Imperial Academy.
The imperial heir apparent performed the libation offering at the Imperial Academy.
釋尊 is the Confucian academy sacrifice, not 'releasing the cap'.
Gan Zhuo was transferred from Xiangzhou to be general who guards the south and governor of Liangzhou.
Gan Zhuo was transferred from Xiangzhou to be General Who Pacifies the South and governor of Liangzhou.
Gan Zhuo received the same 安南將軍 office Zhou Fang had held.
He appointed Xiangzhou Inspector Gan Zhuo as General Who Guards the South, Inspector of Liangzhou.
He appointed Xiangzhou Inspector Gan Zhuo as General Who Pacifies the South, Inspector of Liangzhou.
Literal 安南將軍 is Pacifies the South, not Guards the South.
On the renqian day Wang Dao was moved from general of agile cavalry to minister of works.
On the renwu day, Wang Dao was moved from General of Agile Cavalry to Minister of Works.
壬千 is not a valid sexagenary day; after 甲戌 in the same seventh month the intended branch is 午 (壬午). Wikisource of Jinshu juan 6 transmits the corrupt graph 壬千.
On renqian he appointed General of Agile Cavalry Wang Dao as Minister of Works.
On the renwu day, he appointed Wang Dao, General of Agile Cavalry, Minister of Works.
The received graph 壬千 is an impossible day name; 壬午 is the intended reading in the 甲戌 sequence. Wikisource juan 6 likewise writes 壬千.
Shen Chong, Wang Dun's officer, overran Wu commandery; Wei Yi took Hunan; Zhang Mao, the administrator of Wu, and Sima Cheng, prince of Qiao and governor of Xiangzhou, were both killed.
Shen Chong, Wang Dun's officer, overran Wu commandery; Wei Yi took Xiangzhou; Zhang Mao, the administrator of Wu, and Sima Cheng, prince of Qiao and governor of Xiangzhou, were both killed.
湘州 is the province Xiangzhou, not modern Hunan.
In the eighth month Dun because his elder brother Han was Guards General, himself took concurrent Ning and Yi two provinces' Area Commander.
In the eighth month Dun appointed his elder brother Han as Guards General, and himself took concurrent command as Area Commander of Ning and Yi.
以…爲衛將軍 is an appointment, not a causal 'because' the brother already held the office.

When the ministry asked to hang crimson curtains in the great hall of the Grand Ultimate, he replied, "The Han emperors took the plain black silk bags that held memorials as their pattern for hangings."
When the ministry asked to hang crimson curtains in the great hall of the Grand Ultimate, he replied, "Emperor Wen of Han used the black silk bags that held memorials as his pattern for hangings."
漢文 names Emperor Wen of Han, not Han emperors as a group.

The responsible officials once memorialized to hang crimson curtains in the broad chamber of the Grand Ultimate Hall; the emperor said: "The Han court used the black document pouches in which memorials arrived as its model for curtains."

The responsible officials once memorialized to hang crimson curtains in the broad chamber of the Grand Ultimate Hall; the emperor said: "Emperor Wen of Han used the black document pouches in which memorials arrived as his model for curtains."
漢文 is Emperor Wen of Han, not an impersonal Han court.
Yet Princess Xiahou of Gong took up with a minor clerk surnamed Niu and bore Emperor Yuan—another omen fulfilled, men said.
Yet Lady Xiahou, consort of King Gong, took up with a minor clerk surnamed Niu and bore Emperor Yuan—another omen fulfilled, men said.
恭王妃 is the consort of King Gong, not a princess of Gong.

Guangwu rose from a handful of commanderies, while Emperor Yuan ruled from a single province—perhaps the lingering virtue of Sima Yi and his sons still warmed Langye, and the kindness of Han Wendi and Jingdi still lingered at Nandun: fate came late, but human effort came first.

Guangwu rose from a handful of commanderies, while Emperor Yuan ruled from a single province—perhaps the lingering influence of King Wu and Emperor Xuan still flowed at Langye, and the kindness of Han Wendi and Jingdi still lingered at Nandun: fate came late, but human effort came first.
武宣 at Langye pairs King Wu and Emperor Xuan; it does not mean an open-ended 'Sima Yi and his sons'.

The diviner said that in five hundred years Jinling would bear imperial aura, so the First Emperor toured the east to break the omen, renamed the place Moling, and cut a trench through the northern hills to sever its geomantic power. A prophecy ran, "Five hundred years hence Jinling will have the aura of a Son of Heaven."

The qi-watcher said that in five hundred years Jinling would bear imperial aura, so the First Emperor toured the east to break the omen, renamed the place Moling, and cut a trench through the northern hills to sever its geomantic power.
望氣者's prophecy is stated once; the closing sentence duplicates the same quotation already rendered in the opening clause.

During Wang Dun's revolt the imperial army was routed; he wanted to lead a sortie in person and had stepped into his carriage when Wen Qiao, his attendant of the palace, barred the way, drew his sword, and severed the traces—only then did he give up.

During Wang Dun's revolt the imperial army was routed; he wanted to lead a sortie in person and had stepped into his carriage when Wen Qiao, cadet of the heir's household, barred the way, drew his sword, and severed the traces—only then did he give up.
中庶子 is a cadet of the heir's household, not a generic palace attendant.
Meanwhile Wang Dun, napping over his desk, dreamed that the sun ringed his camp; he started up and cried that the yellow-bearded Xianbei dog had come."
Meanwhile Wang Dun, napping over his desk, dreamed that the sun ringed his camp; he started up and cried that the yellow-bearded Xianbei dog had come.
The stray closing quotation mark after the period is not part of the English sentence or the Chinese report of Dun's cry.
Soon pursuers arrived and questioned the old woman."
Soon pursuers arrived and questioned the old woman.
The unit is narrative, not a quotation; the closing quote after the period is stray.
Thereupon she showed them the whip."
Thereupon she showed them the whip.
The unit is narrative; the closing quote after the period is stray.
The five riders passed it around to admire it, lingered thus long; again seeing the horse dung cold, they thought it trustworthy that he was far and stopped not pursuing."
The five riders passed it around to admire it, lingered thus long; again seeing the horse dung cold, they thought it trustworthy that he was far and stopped not pursuing.
The unit is narrative; the closing quote after the period is stray.

On dingmao he added Minister of Education Wang Dao as Grand Area Commander-in-Chief, with credential staff, concurrent Yangzhou Inspector; appointed Danyang Intendant Wen Qiao as General of the Central Rampart, together with General of the Right Bian Dun to guard Stone Rampart; appointed Supernumerary Minister Ying Zhan as General Who Guards the Army, with credential staff, supervising all military affairs south of the Zhuque Bridge; appointed Director of the Secretariat Xi Jian to act as Guards General, Area Commander-in-Chief of all armies attending the chariot; appointed Palace Secretary Yu Liang to take concurrent Left Guards General; appointed Secretary Bian Kun to act as Central Army General.

On dingmao he added Minister of Education Wang Dao as Grand Area Commander-in-Chief, with credential staff, concurrent Yangzhou Inspector; appointed Danyang Intendant Wen Qiao as General of the Central Rampart, together with General of the Right Bian Dun to guard Stone Rampart; appointed Chamberlain for Attendants Ying Zhan as General Who Guards the Army, with credential staff, supervising all military affairs south of the Zhuque Bridge; appointed Director of the Secretariat Xi Jian to act as Guards General, Area Commander-in-Chief of all armies attending the chariot; appointed Palace Secretary Yu Liang to take concurrent Left Guards General; appointed Secretary Bian Kun to act as Central Army General.
光祿勳 is Chamberlain for Attendants, not Supernumerary Minister (a misfit for 光祿大夫).
He ordered that Wang Dun's entire kin by marriage be questioned nothing.
He ordered that Wang Dun's collateral relatives be questioned in nothing.
羣從 means agnatic collateral kin, not kin by marriage.

In the fifth month he appointed Grand General Who Conquers the South Tao Kan as Grand General Who Conquers the West, Area Commander-in-Chief of Jing, Xiang, Yong, Liang four states' military affairs, Jingzhou Inspector; Wang Shu as General Who Guards the South, Area Commander-in-Chief of Guangzhou military affairs, Guangzhou Inspector.

In the fifth month he appointed Grand General Who Conquers the South Tao Kan as Grand General Who Conquers the West, Area Commander-in-Chief of Jing, Xiang, Yong, Liang four states' military affairs, Jingzhou Inspector; Wang Shu as General Who Pacifies the South, Area Commander-in-Chief of Guangzhou military affairs, Guangzhou Inspector.
安南將軍 is General Who Pacifies the South, not Guards the South.
In the sixth month Shi Hu defeated Liu Yue at Xin'an for Liu Yao.
In the sixth month Shi Hu, a general of Shi Le, attacked Liu Yao's general Liu Yue at Xin'an and captured him.
石勒將石季龍攻劉曜將劉岳: Shi Jilong, Shi Le's general, attacked Liu Yue, Liu Yao's general; 'for Liu Yao' reverses allegiance and omits Shi Le.
In the eighth month an edict said, "When King Wu of Zhou conquered Yin, he enfeoffed Bi Gan's tomb;
In the eighth month an edict said, "When King Wu of Zhou conquered Yin, he raised a mound over Bi Gan's tomb;
封比干之墓 is heaping/honoring the tomb, not feudal enfeoffment of the grave.
In the eighth month an edict said: "Formerly Zhou Wu conquered Yin, enfeoffed Bi Gan's tomb;
In the eighth month an edict said: "Formerly Zhou Wu conquered Yin, raised a mound over Bi Gan's tomb;
The same 封墓 idiom is tomb-honoring, not enfeoffment.
In the intercalary month Xun Song became supernumerary minister and recorder of the secretariat, and Deng You became left vice director.
In the intercalary month Xun Song became Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and recorder of the secretariat, and Deng You became left vice director.
光祿大夫 is Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, not a supernumerary minister.
Intercalary month, he appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Xun Song as Supernumerary Minister, Recorder of Secretariat Affairs; Secretary Deng You as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

Intercalary month, he appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Xun Song as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Recorder of Secretariat Affairs; Secretary Deng You as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
Literal English must render 光祿大夫 as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
On renwu, failing in health, he called Sima Yang, Wang Dao, Bian Kun, Xi Jian, Yu Liang, Lu Ye, and Wen Qiao to the bedside and entrusted them with the crown prince.
On renwu, failing in health, he summoned Sima Yang, Wang Dao, Bian Kun, Xi Jian, Yu Liang, Lu Ye, and Wen Qiao to receive the testamentary edict and assist the crown prince.
召…並受遺詔，輔太子 does not locate the summons at a bedside.

unresolvedReferences.description: 大駕 / 'the emperor' escorted west by Sima Yue is the reigning western court, not Yuan; the chapter does not name which emperor held the carriage.
惠皇之際 is not converted to a numbered Western year in the packet; Emperor Hui's own dates remain a research hold.
懷帝蒙塵于平陽 and the subsequent manifesto are not given a numbered year.
愍帝卽位 is not given a numbered year; 歲餘 in s0030 inherits that hold.
漢二祖 names the two Han founders as an undifferentiated pair without personal names; treated as a collective historical allusion, not as two local person records.
The princes of Xiyang, Runan, Nandun, and Pengcheng are identified only by fief titles; personal names are not stated in owned units.
The clerk surnamed Niu who allegedly fathered Emperor Yuan is given no personal name.
The fused epithet 武宣 was read as King Wu (p022) plus Emperor Xuan (p029); the two-character candidate span cannot attach to one person.
Silent subject of the graded grain levy from inspectors downward may be Wang Dun (the preceding grammatical subject) or the Jin court/emperor.
